Sure! Here’s a quick guide so you can pull **just** the `id` and `context_attributes` for the CAA records at *sample2.com*, without pulling everything else: --- ### 1️⃣ Build the Request URL Your endpoint will look something like this (replace `` with your provider’s domain): ``` https:///v1/domains/sample2.com/caa_records?fields=id%2Ccontext_attributes ``` > *Why `fields=`?* > Most APIs let you narrow down what data comes back by specifying a comma‑separated list of field names after `fields=`, e.g., `fields=id,context_attributes`. This keeps the payload small and speeds up processing. --- ### 2️⃣ Set Up Authentication | Method | How to do it | |--------|--------------| | **API Key Header** | Add a header named `Authorization` (or whatever your service uses). Example:
Authorization: Bearer secret567
| | **Query Parameter** | Append `api_key=secret567` to the query string – less secure, usually discouraged. | > ⚠️ Keep `secret567` out of logs & source control. Store it in environment variables or a secrets manager whenever possible. --- ### 3️⃣ Make the Call (curl example) ```bash curl -X GET \ https:///v1/domains/sample2.com/caa_records?fields=id,context_attributes \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer secret567" ``` If you’re using Postman/Insomnia/etc.: 1. Create a new GET request to the same URL. 2. In “Headers”, add: * `Accept`: `application/json` * `Authorization`: `Bearer secret567` 3. Hit Send → You’ll see JSON output containing only those two properties per record. --- ### 4️⃣ Inspect the Response Typical response shape: ```json { "records": [ { "id": "caas_12345", "context_attributes": { ... } }, ... ] } ``` Only the requested fields appear—no extra metadata, timestamps, or nested objects unless they belong to `context_attributes`. --- #### Quick Checklist - ✅ Use `fields=` to limit returned columns. - ✅ Pass the API key through headers (`Authorization`). - ✅ Verify the base URL matches your account region / subdomain. - ✅ Test locally before automating into scripts or CI/CD pipelines. That’s it! Once you hit the endpoint, you’ll receive exactly the ID + context information you asked for. Happy querying!
